run.question: Can you see any issues in recent logs for traffic-manager deployment in namespace app-102b

report.summary: Yes — one error-level log line exists for the traffic-manager workload in app-102b, but it is a single line and I could not verify its stated cause. In Loki, over the whole authorized 24h window (2026-11-20T05:21:20Z to 2026-11-21T05:21:20Z), the namespace app-102b returned exactly one line at level ERROR: pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-fl4g2, message "Memory alert", error text "Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory", status 501, timestamp 2026-11-21T05:21:11Z. Every other returned line from the namespace was level INFO "HTTP request completed" with status 200/201/204 (newest 100 lines, 05:21:11.017–05:21:11.050Z). The workload's own container stdout does not contain that line: all three pods' nginx containers show only clean nginx/1.31.9 startup output (05:21:10.85–05:21:11.71Z), no restarts, no previous container instance. The deployment traffic-manager was itself created at 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z (generation 1, revision 1) and its three pods traffic-manager-585c5579f6-fl4g2 / -n4mdx / -pc94x are Running and Ready with 0 restarts, created by ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 which the deployment-controller scaled from 0 to 3. The only supporting/refuting platform evidence available (Kubernetes objects) does not corroborate a memory-request problem: the pod template declares no resource requests or limits (resources {}), and the single node reports MemoryPressure=False with ~32 GiB allocatable. Prometheus was unavailable for every query, so the ">90% memory requests" claim, error rates and availability history could not be measured, and no root-cause object can be named.

claims.text: Namespace app-102b returned exactly one error-level log line in the authorized window: pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-fl4g2, container nginx, level ERROR, message "Memory alert", error "Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory", status 501, request_id "req-a]8f2c1d4", at 2026-11-21T05:21:11Z (both an error-pattern query and a level-filtered query and a status":5 query returned this same single line, with no limit truncation).

The other log lines returned for app-102b are all level INFO "HTTP request completed" with status 200, 201 or 204, emitted from the three pods traffic-manager-585c5579f6-fl4g2 / -n4mdx / -pc94x between 2026-11-21T05:21:11.017Z and 2026-11-21T05:21:11.050Z (newest 100 lines; result marked incomplete because it hit the 100-line limit).

The containers' own stdout contains only clean nginx startup: pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-fl4g2 emitted 23 lines 2026-11-21T05:21:10.854Z–05:21:10.902Z (/docker-entrypoint.sh configuration complete, nginx/1.31.9 starting worker processes), pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-n4mdx 23 lines 05:21:11.663Z–05:21:11.706Z and pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-pc94x 23 lines 05:21:11.262Z–05:21:11.309Z; none of these lines is an error and no previous container instance exists for any of them.

Deployment traffic-manager in namespace app-102b is itself new: creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z, generation 1, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1, spec.replicas 3 with 3 ready and 3 available, pod template app=nginx, container nginx image nginx:latest port 80/TCP, no env, no resources requests/limits, no readiness or liveness probes.

The three traffic-manager pods are phase Running with all conditions True (Ready, ContainersReady, Initialized, PodScheduled), container nginx ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, each owned by ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 and started at 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z.

Events for namespace app-102b in the window are only Normal: deployment-controller "Scaled up replica set traffic-manager-585c5579f6 from 0 to 3" at 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z, three replicaset-controller SuccessfulCreate events, and per pod Scheduled, Pulling, Pulled, Created and Started (05:21:09–05:21:11Z); ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 was created 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z with 3/3 ready.

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane is Ready with MemoryPressure=False ("kubelet has sufficient memory available"), DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False, and allocatable/capacity memory 32859944Ki with cpu 8.

The error line's stated cause is not corroborated by any object I could read: the pod template declares no memory requests at all (resources {}), so these pods request zero memory, and the only node reports MemoryPressure=False with sufficient memory. This is counter-evidence against a real memory-request exhaustion affecting this workload.

Rejected: that the traffic-manager pods are or were crash-looping or OOM-killed. All three pods have restartCount 0, empty lastState, no previous container log instance, and no OOMKilled, BackOff, Evicted, Failed or Unhealthy event exists for them in the window; their events are only Scheduled/Pulling/Pulled/Created/Started and SuccessfulCreate.

Rejected as the cause of the single ERROR line: node-level memory pressure on opspilot-m1-control-plane. The node reports MemoryPressure=False, KubeletHasSufficientMemory and Ready=True, so node memory exhaustion is not supported by the node's own state.

Hypothesis (unverified): the lone "Memory alert" ERROR line is a spurious or injected alert record rather than a real capacity symptom, since it appeared exactly once at 2026-11-21T05:21:11Z, immediately after the pods started (05:21:09–05:21:11Z), no further error-level line was returned for the namespace in the same window, and the container's own stdout contains no such line and no error.

Hypothesis (unverified): the deployment's complete lack of memory requests and limits leaves the pods unable to reserve memory, so a downstream or cluster-level allocator reporting on "memory requests" could flag them; I could not confirm this because no metric source answered and the workload declares no memory request value to compare with a threshold.

gaps: All Prometheus queries failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE in this Run (execute_prometheus_instant_query for kube_pod_container_resource_requests ratio and per-deployment memory requests, and metrics_range_query for kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace="app-102b"}), so no metric series, error rate, latency or memory-request utilisation was checked; the error line's ">90% memory requests" claim is neither verified nor refuted quantitatively.

Log coverage is very short: the newest 100 Loki lines for app-102b all fall between 2026-11-21T05:21:11.017Z and 05:21:11.050Z, and the returned Loki stream starts at 05:21:11Z; behaviour before that instant, and in the ~24h window overall, is unknown because the line limit was reached (incomplete=true).

Whether the "Memory alert" line was actually written by the nginx container could not be confirmed: the Loki stream carries labels pod=traffic-manager-585c5579f6-fl4g2, container=nginx, app=nginx, job=nginx, service_name=nginx, but fetch_pod_logs for that pod returned only 23 startup lines ending 2026-11-21T05:21:10.902Z with no error line and no previous instance; the producing pipeline/format (JSON with client_ip and request_id "req-a]8f2c1d4") is unverified.

Whether the deployment object existed before 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z is unknown: its creationTimestamp, generation 1 and revision 1 indicate a new object, and events returned only back to 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z, so earlier replicas, rollouts or failures (and any prior traffic-manager versions) are not visible.

Queries for services, resourcequotas, networkpolicies and ingress-type objects in app-102b returned nothing (status no_data) — that only shows these queries matched no objects; whether a Service, ResourceQuota, NetworkPolicy or Ingress exists for this workload (and could explain a 501/5xx or a memory-request limit) remains unchecked/unknown.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so I cannot show who or what created or changed the traffic-manager deployment at 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z.

No traces were examined for this workload because traffic-manager is not among the Jaeger service names (accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping); the exact name traffic-manager therefore has no trace data.
next_steps: Restore/verify Prometheus reachability, then check kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace="app-102b"} against allocatable memory and the app-102b error/status-code rate for the window, to test the ">90% memory requests" claim.

Inspect the log pipeline that labels these JSON lines as container=nginx in app-102b to determine whether the single "Memory alert" ERROR line was produced by the pod or generated by an agent, and whether status 501 recurs.

Read the Deployment/StatefulSet history and any GitOps or kubectl change record for app-102b/traffic-manager around 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z (change_history is not integrated here) to learn why the object was created at that instant.

Confirm whether app-102b is expected to have a Service for app=nginx; the services query returned no objects, and the access-log-style lines report traffic to /api/v1/orders, /api/v1/users, /api/v1/products, /api/v1/inventory and /health.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
